newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to try $2,400, aluminium to follow.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to try $2,400, aluminium to follow.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are likely to re-challenge overhead targets in the $2,400/2,405 level again on Monday against the background of a strong yen.
Analysts said aluminium was also likely to push higher, aided also by a fall in LME stocks and expectations of constructive IPAI data later this morning.
COPPER -
The market has already tried to test $2,400, but again the resistance is making itself felt.
Yet the upside looks favourable if this level can be eroded, traders said.
"For the moment prices are holding below $2,400 - a breach of $2,407 would signal $2,440, our nearby target," William Adams of LME trader Rudolf Wolf and Co said.

Developments in the backwardation and stocks will continue to provide short-term pointers. Cash/threes is currently stable at a $55/60 premium, while the pace of stock increases, due to previous high backwardations, is slowing, traders noted.
Technically, the indicators are trending higher, but not sending out adverse signals.
"With the RSI at 69 (percent) and stochastics at 69, the market is not overbought yet," Adams said.
At 0856 gmt copper was quoted at $2,386/2,390, little-changed from pre-weekend levels.
ALUMINIUM -
Prices are attempting to clear resistance around $1,670/672 in order to push into fresh upside territory.
"Clearance of $1,672 would target $1,707. We would look for aluminium to then consolidate before breaking higher again," Wolff's Adams said.
Should the market ease back if the overhead challenge falls, then there is good support available around $1,640.
At 0856 gmt aluminium was indicated at $1,672/1,674, up some $11 from Friday.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
